spot.html_text: a “humanist” opposition to scientific positivism and materialist determinism for its neglect of the subjective dimension to human action. Here he was influenced by neo-idealist philosophers and critics of the classical Marxist tradition, primarily Benedetto Croce; a radical insistence on the force of subjectively motivated collective action, expressed as the formation of a unified moral will. The most popular source of this view in Italy was the revolutionary syndicalist thinker, Georges Sorel;
